newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Alberta sets March 11 provincial election.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Alberta sets March 11 provincial election.

text.p: Alberta Premier Ralph Klein said on Tuesday that a general election in the petroleum-rich Canadian province would be held on March 11.
The election call came after Klein's ruling Conservative government delivered a budget that projected a fourth consecutive surplus while boosting spending on squeezed social programs.

Political observers have forecast the Conservatives -- who have chopped government spending over the past four years by 20 percent amid an economic boom driven by a robust energy sector -- would handily regain their majority in the provincial legislature.
Recent polls have placed Klein's approval rating among Albertans as high as 69 percent.

An Angus Reid/Southam News poll released on Tuesday showed 63 percent of voters who made a decision favored the Klein Conservatives, 24 percent favored the opposition Liberal Party and 11 percent backed the left-leaning New Democrats.

The government on Tuesday estimated a 1997-98 budget surplus that could top C$800 million if oil and natural gas prices exceeded assumptions of US$19 per barrel for West Texas Intermediate crude oil and C$1.55 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas at the wellhead.
That would follow an estimated 1996-97 surplus of over C$2.2 billion.

With an election looming and concerns growing among many voters over budget cuts, especially in health care, the government also announced its first increase in spending since 1993. In a move that Klein has termed "re-investment," health-care spending was forecast to increase by C$128 million, education spending by C$91 million and expenditures for senior-citizen programs by C$180 million.

Klein, who was a popular mayor of Calgary during the 1980s, came to provincial power in late 1992 after the resignation of former Conservative Premier Don Getty. He won a landslide victory in an election held a few months later.
